Precondition: A machined line has open Good castings at its cell and a published SubAssembly BOM consuming that casting
Step: Trigger Machining OUT for a piece count and scan a fresh LTT
Expected Result: A new SubAssembly part-number LOT is minted (its own PieceCount, status, location) carrying a genealogy edge back to the source casting
Notes: Machining OUT is a consume-MINT (Workorder.MachiningOut_Mint), not a rename and not a plain same-part split

Precondition: Multiple open same-part castings sit at the cell with different arrival times
Step: Mint a SubAssembly for a quantity spanning more than one casting
Expected Result: Consumption is strict oldest-first (FIFO arrival order) across all open same-part castings at the cell, rolling into the next as each empties; no casting is driven negative

Precondition: A mint consumes two source castings
Step: Complete the mint and inspect genealogy
Expected Result: One ConsumptionEvent + Consumption genealogy edge + closure row is written per source casting (multi-parent traceability); minted LOT is named <oldest-casting-LTT>-NN

Precondition: The source casting is a child line on line-eligible published SubAssembly BOM(s)
Step: Trigger the mint without specifying a produced part
Expected Result: The produced SubAssembly part is auto-derived via BOM child->parent + line eligibility; if more than one producible part matches, the mint is rejected until a ProducedItemId is specified

Precondition: Requested mint exceeds producible pieces from available castings; partial not allowed
Step: Request a mint larger than can be produced
Expected Result: Mint is rejected and the system reports Available = the maximum producible quantity

Precondition: Requested mint exceeds producible pieces; partial allowed
Step: Request the oversized mint with partial allowed
Expected Result: System mints floor(totalAvailable / QtyPer); the un-consumed balance stays on the open source castings for a later draw

Precondition: A minted SubAssembly LOT with a recorded consume-mint
Step: Open the genealogy view and trace both directions
Expected Result: Minted LOT -> source castings and casting -> minted children are both queryable; the genealogy edge + closure are permanent and immutable
Notes: Machining OUT edges are Consumption (RelationshipTypeId=3), not Split, in the current consume-mint model

Precondition: A trimmed LOT sits in local Trim Storage and is eligible for this line
Step: Pick/claim the LOT at Machining IN
Expected Result: The SAME LOT is claimed onto the line and a MachiningIn checkpoint ProductionEvent is recorded; the LOT keeps its identity, item, status and piece count - NO new LOT, NO ConsumptionEvent, NO rename at IN
Notes: Trim->Machining rename-via-1-line-BOM is RETIRED; identity change now happens at the Machining OUT mint (FDS-05-009). FDS-05-033 title is stale.

Precondition: Trimmed LOTs deposited in this shop's Trim Storage
Step: Inspect the line's Machining IN queue
Expected Result: Queue surfaces the Trim-Storage LOTs eligible for this line, ordered FIFO by arrival (LotMovement.MovedAt)

Precondition: An eligible LOT shows in the Machining IN queue
Step: Claim the next LOT to this line
Expected Result: In one transaction the whole LOT is moved Trim Storage -> line and a MachiningIn checkpoint is written; the LOT then drops off every other line's queue

Precondition: Two lines see the same Trim-Storage LOT and another line claims it first
Step: Attempt to claim the already-claimed LOT
Expected Result: Claim is rejected cleanly (LOT was just claimed by another line); no checkpoint written

Precondition: A Trim-Storage LOT whose part is NOT eligible at this line
Step: Attempt to claim it to this line
Expected Result: Claim is rejected - the part is not eligible at this line (authoritative server-side gate)

Precondition: A LOT in process at a machining line
Step: Record a machining production event (submit counters)
Expected Result: A Workorder.ProductionEvent checkpoint is written against the LOT with cumulative counters, operator, terminal and timestamp

Precondition: Recording a machining event with rejects
Step: Enter one or more defect codes with reject quantities and submit
Expected Result: A RejectEvent row is written for each defect code used

Precondition: Machining screen open
Step: Look for any operator-facing Work Order create/select/login on the machining screen
Expected Result: None present - Production work orders are auto-generated background bookkeeping, invisible to operators

Precondition: Database access to the Workorder schema
Step: Inspect the Workorder.WorkOrder table structure
Expected Result: Schema carries WorkOrderType, ItemId, RouteTemplateId, ToolId (nullable), WorkOrderStatus; work-order operations track per route step

Precondition: A LOT processed through machining with no work order
Step: Record production/consumption/reject evidence and inspect the rows
Expected Result: ProductionEvent / ConsumptionEvent / RejectEvent are written with WorkOrderOperationId NULL - the evidence layer functions standalone

Precondition: Fresh migrated database
Step: Query Workorder.WorkOrderType
Expected Result: Exactly one active row is seeded: Production; Demand and Maintenance are FUTURE and NOT seeded

Precondition: Database access to Workorder.WorkOrder
Step: Inspect the shipped columns against the live-flag decision
Expected Result: Only Flexware flags confirmed live with MPP ship as columns; dead flags are absent

Precondition: A machining line configured to mint a SubAssembly
Step: Trigger Machining OUT for the line
Expected Result: Machining OUT mints the SubAssembly via route-driven consume-mint; mints are line-resident
Notes: FDS-06-008 title mentions auto-move to a coupled assembly cell — that cell-coupling mechanism is RETIRED; no cell->cell auto-move
